title: Can every fixed-dimensional Tarski problem be solved with O(log² n) queries?
question: Let Q(n,k) be the minimum worst-case number of adaptive deterministic value queries needed to find any fixed point of an unknown monotone function $f:[n]^k\to[n]^k$, where [n]={1,...,n} and monotonicity is with respect to coordinatewise order. A query at x reveals the entire vector f(x). Is it true that for every integer k>=1 there is a constant C_k such that $Q(n,k)\le C_k(1+\log_2 n)^2$ for every n>=2? Arbitrary finite computation between queries is allowed. Constants may depend on k but not on n or f. This asks for an exponent independent of the fixed dimension, not a polynomial bound on C_k.
